story.headline: Students reported vacating Satya Niketan PGs after Delhi building collapse
story.body:
Students in Delhi's Satya Niketan area are moving out of paying guest accommodations and rented rooms following a building collapse in the neighbourhood, according to a News18 Hindi report published on September 9.

News18 Hindi reported that PG accommodations in the area are emptying one by one, and quoted the sentiment among residents as being that they can no longer continue living there. The outlet reported that some students have been spending nights at their colleges.

The intake note received on the desk carries the same broad outline: that frightened students are leaving their lodgings in the wake of the collapse, with colleges serving as a stopgap for some.

No casualty figure, no date or time for the collapse itself, and no identification of the building involved has been established from the material available to this desk. The number of PGs affected and the number of students who have moved out are also not confirmed.

No statement from Delhi civic authorities, the police, PG operators or college administrations is available in the material on hand, and none should be characterised until obtained directly.

Before publication, the desk needs to independently confirm: when and where exactly the collapse occurred; whether there were injuries or deaths; the identity and status of the collapsed structure; the scale of the exodus from local PGs; whether any official inspection, evacuation order or safety notice has been issued for buildings in Satya Niketan; and on-the-record comment from students, PG owners, colleges and the relevant municipal body. Direct student quotes must be gathered by our own reporter rather than carried over from another outlet.

blocks.label: Headline
lines: दिल्ली में इमारत गिरने के बाद सत्य निकेतन के पीजी खाली कर रहे छात्र

blocks.label: Body
lines: न्यूज18 हिंदी की 9 सितंबर को प्रकाशित एक रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, दिल्ली के सत्य निकेतन इलाके में एक इमारत गिरने के बाद छात्र पेइंग गेस्ट (पीजी) आवासों और किराए के कमरों से बाहर निकल रहे हैं।

न्यूज18 हिंदी ने बताया कि इलाके के पीजी एक-एक कर खाली हो रहे हैं, और वहां रहने वालों की भावना को इस रूप में उद्धृत किया कि वे अब वहां रहना जारी नहीं रख सकते। रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक कुछ छात्र रातें अपने कॉलेजों में बिता रहे हैं।
डेस्क को मिले इनटेक नोट में भी यही मोटा खाका है: कि इमारत गिरने के बाद डरे हुए छात्र अपने ठिकाने छोड़ रहे हैं, और कुछ के लिए कॉलेज अस्थायी सहारा बने हुए हैं।

इस डेस्क के पास उपलब्ध सामग्री से न तो हताहतों की कोई संख्या स्थापित हुई है, न ही इमारत गिरने की तारीख या समय, और न ही संबंधित इमारत की पहचान। कितने पीजी प्रभावित हुए और कितने छात्र वहां से जा चुके हैं, इसकी भी पुष्टि नहीं हुई है।

उपलब्ध सामग्री में दिल्ली के नागरिक अधिकारियों, पुलिस, पीजी संचालकों या कॉलेज प्रशासनों का कोई बयान मौजूद नहीं है, और जब तक सीधे तौर पर हासिल न हो, किसी भी पक्ष के रुख के बारे में कुछ नहीं कहा जाना चाहिए।

प्रकाशन से पहले डेस्क को स्वतंत्र रूप से इनकी पुष्टि करनी होगी: इमारत ठीक कब और कहां गिरी; कोई घायल हुआ या किसी की मौत हुई; गिरी हुई संरचना की पहचान और स्थिति क्या है; स्थानीय पीजी से पलायन का पैमाना क्या है; सत्य निकेतन की इमारतों के लिए कोई सरकारी निरीक्षण, खाली कराने का आदेश या सुरक्षा नोटिस जारी हुआ है या नहीं; और छात्रों, पीजी मालिकों, कॉलेजों तथा संबंधित नगर निकाय की ऑन-द-रिकॉर्ड प्रतिक्रिया। छात्रों के सीधे उद्धरण किसी दूसरे संस्थान से लिए जाने के बजाय हमारे अपने रिपोर्टर द्वारा जुटाए जाने चाहिए।

brief.headline: Students reported vacating Satya Niketan PGs after Delhi building collapse
brief.body:
Students in Delhi's Satya Niketan area are moving out of paying guest accommodations and rented rooms following a building collapse in the neighbourhood, according to a News18 Hindi report published on September 9.

News18 Hindi reported that PG accommodations in the area are emptying one by one, and quoted the sentiment among residents as being that they can no longer continue living there. The outlet reported that some students have been spending nights at their colleges.

The intake note received on the desk carries the same broad outline: that frightened students are leaving their lodgings in the wake of the collapse, with colleges serving as a stopgap for some.

No casualty figure, no date or time for the collapse itself, and no identification of the building involved has been established from the material available to this desk. The number of PGs affected and the number of students who have moved out are also not confirmed.

No statement from Delhi civic authorities, the police, PG operators or college administrations is available in the material on hand, and none should be characterised until obtained directly.

Before publication, the desk needs to independently confirm: when and where exactly the collapse occurred; whether there were injuries or deaths; the identity and status of the collapsed structure; the scale of the exodus from local PGs; whether any official inspection, evacuation order or safety notice has been issued for buildings in Satya Niketan; and on-the-record comment from students, PG owners, colleges and the relevant municipal body. Direct student quotes must be gathered by our own reporter rather than carried over from another outlet.
